decisions.statement: The line the cursor sits on is read before the newline is sent.
That line is read off the pane of the tmux session the seat is.
The row read is the one tmux says the pane's cursor sits on.
A prompt row opens with two columns of the prompt's own marker.
The line is that row past those two columns.
A pane in copy mode answers no line.
A terminal holding no seat opens a line carrying nothing.
A line tmux does not answer opens a line carrying nothing.
The editor is handed in rather than imported.
A line the prompt wrapped opens a line carrying that line's own prefix.
No tab reaches the prompt, so no indent read off it is a tab.
No key other than the one opening a line is read here.
Nothing here sweeps the terminals for their seats.
The prompt drops a newline carried in a bracketed paste and joins what sits either side of it.
The newline is escape then return, which is the key the prompt opens a line on.
The newline and the prefix are sent as one write, so no gap is left between the two.

definition: the key opening a line in a seat's terminal, sent with the prefix it carries
